subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a Keeper of the Tome who was murdered after being struck in the face, falling forward and chipping a tooth, and then having his heart torn out and his ribcage smashed, with blackened finger and lip indicating he had been reading a poisoned page and wetting his fingertip on his lip.
source_quote: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was laid out before us, and the early findings were already on the table. The heart was gone — torn out, not for any wound it would cause, but as a guard against any working that calls the dead back to answer. The tip of his left forefinger was blackened. Not blue. Darker than blue. And the same dark smudge sat dead-center on his lower lip.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi had been taking notes in blue ink at the time of his death, with fresh stains on his right sleeve — the working hand — and a chip in one front tooth from a forward fall.
source_quote: Clotted blood under the nose. Smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic — the *right* sleeve, the working hand. And blotches of midnight blue across the cuff. I knew that blue. 'Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books?' It was. Janussi had been taking notes when this happened. Writing hand, fresh stains. A man interrupted at work. And a chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi’s tongue was blackened at the tip, confirming ingestion of the black substance, and his nose was broken before death, as bruising cannot form on a corpse.
source_quote: The tongue, blackened at the tip — ingestion confirmed twice over now. And a chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent. Not an old break worn smooth, but a fresh wound. The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed. My focus narrowed and held, and the picture came clear and certain: this happened before he died.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber contained a silver pedestal, an ebony pipe with cherry tobacco, an open safe with scattered empty pouches, loose sapphires, and scraps of parchment naming spells, with four sealed pouches, a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, a potion of water breathing, five diamonds, platinum, and gold left untouched.
source_quote: The safe. A box of metal as wide as a man's reach, sunk into the tower wall, its door standing open. Empty pouches scattered in front of it, sapphires loose and dazzling, scraps of parchment naming spells. But still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber held an armchair with three circular impacts and two holes punched clean through the back, indicating darts of pure force had been fired at it, not at the body.
source_quote: Daz drifted to the armchair next, and read the wounds in it the way he'd read the wounds in the man. Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. He studied it and pronounced it: darts of pure force. Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks. Somebody had aimed three bolts of force at a chair.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: A three-foot marble statue of the hooded bearded old man holding a candle aloft — the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore — was toppled near the armchairs and tea table, having been knocked over in shock upon discovering the body.
source_quote: Last, the statue. Three feet of marble, a hooded bearded old man holding a candle aloft, toppled on the floor near the armchairs and the tea table. The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: the black substance
fact: The black substance found on Janussi’s finger, lip, and tongue was not ink, not poison from his inkwell, and was unidentifiable even by Glabbagool, an ooze that has ingested the Underdark — indicating it was something uniquely dangerous and unnatural.
source_quote: Darkness than blue. That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*. Darker than anything in his inkwell. Zalthir, ever the auditor of other people's competence, pushed on it — *our great detective took his long, careful look and still can't tell us if it's ink?* No. That was exactly what I could tell. The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*. Would't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark? We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name. But even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered.

subject: the locket
fact: A locket or necklace was torn from Janussi’s neck, leaving broken lead links and worn impressions where it had hung, suggesting it was a personal, long-carried item of significance.
source_quote: The neck told us more. The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him. A locket, a necklace — gone, snapped at the chain. I have catalogued a great many sacred spaces in my time, and there is a particular grief in an empty setting where something belonged. The links were worn where it had hung. Whatever it was, he'd carried it a long time.

subject: the missing sapphire
fact: One sapphire was missing from the safe, while four others remained sealed in pouches, indicating the thief sought not treasure but a specific component for a spell requiring a single sapphire.
source_quote: But one sapphire was missing. One parchment. 'Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell,' he said, 'a spell that requires a sapphire.' And here is where the room stopped making sense as a robbery. Because still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: The Discoveries
fact: The spellbook *The Discoveries* was the last thing Janussi wrote in, with fresh blue ink noting unfamiliar spells, and its entries were newer than those in *The Golden Ass*, confirming it was his final act before death.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it. There was more than one color on those pages, and I wanted the newest one isolated before anything else. The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.* 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation. The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: Janussi's death sequence
fact: Janussi was assaulted before death — struck in the face, breaking his nose — then returned to his desk, wrote in *The Discoveries*, read a poisoned page, wetted his fingertip on his lip, fell forward, chipping his tooth, and was later found and desecrated by a deliberate, unhurried killer who removed his heart and took one sapphire and a locket.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. The black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: the attack on the armchair
fact: Three darts of pure force were fired at the armchair in the Keeper's Chamber, missing Janussi entirely, suggesting the attacker was enraged but not targeting the Keeper directly at that moment.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. He studied it and pronounced it: darts of pure force. Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks. Somebody had aimed three bolts of force at a chair.

subject: the discovery of the body
fact: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore discovered the body at dawn and knocked over the marble statue of himself in shock, an accidental disruption to the scene.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: the theft from the safe
fact: The safe was opened without force, and only one sapphire and one parchment were taken, while a vast treasure remained untouched, indicating the thief had a precise, non-greedy objective.
source_quote: The killer had the combination, or had no need of one. In other words, score what they left them. A small fortune, untouched. Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: Glabbagool's failed analysis
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze that has consumed the Underdark, could not identify the black substance on Janussi’s body, confirming it was an unknown and exceptionally dangerous material.
source_quote: We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name. But even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered. When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: Keeper's Desk
fact: The Keeper's Desk held blue ink, *The Discoveries*, *The Golden Ass*, and other writing materials, with the blue ink in *The Discoveries* being the most recent, indicating Janussi’s final intellectual activity before death.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it. The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: the ebony pipe with cherry tobacco
fact: An ebony pipe with cherry tobacco was found on the desk, suggesting the killer may have used smoke to mask the odor of poison.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco. Pretty, until Zalthir's instinct landed it — tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: the interrogation of the statue
fact: Thorin expressed fear that the statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore might awaken, causing Tadric to become unnerved, though the statue had merely been knocked over accidentally.
source_quote: 'Shake the candle,' Thorin said. 'I don't want it to wake up and attack us,' Thorin explained. 'I've had, you know, had bad experiences.' It worked on poor Tadric exactly as you'd fear. He tried not to look at the candle and then could not stop looking at the candle, and finally turned to Thorin. 'Are you sure this — is it true about candles?'
